chapter: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
title: Catskills gig at Woodbourne and staying in New York
summary: Hall is called with baritonist Fathead Lawrence to replace Erskine Hawkins's rhythm section in the mountains and then stays in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. So you made the trip to New York with Tiny Bradshaw and you're back to Philly, and let's see that was '34 and then what happened?
'34. I guess the kind of run into one another We got some dates (unintelligible) because when I left Les Robinson at the Club Harlem I came to the Catskills.
You went to the Catskill Mountains?
How did you happen to go up there?
I got a wire, got a call.

The rhythm section of the Erskine Hawkins band had been off and they were working there. Lowell Morgan [Staufield] who is still around, and the bass player's name, Lee and the drummer, and Erskine has a gig and so they have to come back and they need a replacement so Fathead Lawrence have to look that up too, he's a hell of a baritone, played without a strap.
Must have had some strong hands.

Terrific. He and I were called from Philadelphia to make the gig in Woodbourne. So we went to Woodbourne and the mountains weren't too populated at that point, so the gig closed before Labor Day, and we came back to New York. He was from Hampton, Virginia, he went to Virginia and I came to New York.
Fathead Lawrence, and that's how I stayed in New York.
Yeah. I never went back to Philly.
